subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure on the span of an orthonormal n-frame is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Put ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i (s_i the coordinates of s ∈ ℝ^n = Euclid n), and Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. Then the n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure H^n = μHE[n] restricted to Q is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure L^n (volume on ℝ^n) under ι: H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n), i.e. μHE[n].restrict Q = Measure.map ι volume.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) = Measure.map (fun s : Euclid n => ∑ i, s i • τ i) volume
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent-supplied proof ("H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n) (μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n; Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume)"), stated as a separate lemma because the transfer between the plane Q and the parameter space ℝ^n is used repeatedly in the sibling plane_constancy_reduction. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; L^n := volume on ℝ^n = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); s_i are the coordinates of s ∈ ℝ^n; ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i; Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. Nothing is assumed about n or P beyond τ being orthonormal (n = 0 is allowed: then Q = {0} and ι is the map from the one-point space ℝ^0 to 0).
1. (ι is a linear isometry.) ι is linear (ι(s + t) = ι(s) + ι(t), ι(cs) = cι(s)). For s ∈ ℝ^n, orthonormality gives ⟨ι(s), ι(s)⟩ = Σ_{i,k} s_i s_k ⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩ = Σ_i s_i² = ‖s‖² (Mathlib Orthonormal.inner_sum together with the Euclidean norm formula EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖ for all s, and, ι being additive, ‖ι(s) − ι(t)‖ = ‖ι(s − t)‖ = ‖s − t‖: ι is an isometry (AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm).
2. (range ι = Q.) Each ι(s) = Σ_i s_i τ_i is a linear combination of τ_1, …, τ_n, hence lies in Q. Conversely, every y ∈ Q = span{τ_1, …, τ_n} can be written y = Σ_i c_i τ_i with c : Fin n → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), i.e. y = ι(c) where c is regarded as the element of ℝ^n with coordinates c_i. So range ι = Q.
3. (Isometry invariance of μHE[n].) For an isometry f : X → Y between metric spaces carrying their Borel σ-algebras, the push-forward of μHE[d] under f is μHE[d] restricted to the range of f: (μHE[d]).map f = μHE[d].restrict (range f) (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; it expresses H^d(f(A)) = H^d(A), the isometry invariance of Hausdorff measure, together with the fact that f is a measurable embedding with image range f). Applying it to ι (step 1) with d = n and using step 2: (μHE[n] on ℝ^n).map ι = μHE[n].restrict (range ι) = μHE[n].restrict Q.
4. (Normalization.) On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) the measure μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure: μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; the normalizing factor in the definition of μHE[n] is chosen exactly so that this holds).
5. (Conclusion.) Substituting 4 into 3: μHE[n].restrict Q = volume.map ι = Measure.map ι volume, i.e. H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n). ∎

  intro P n τ hτ
  let L : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P :=
    { toFun := fun s => ∑ i, s i • τ i
      map_add' := fun s t => by simp [add_smul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      map_smul' := fun c s => by simp [Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul] }
  have hLapp : ∀ s, L s = ∑ i, s i • τ i := fun s => rfl
  have hnorm : ∀ s, ‖L s‖ = ‖s‖ := by
    intro s
    have h1 : ‖L s‖ ^ 2 = ‖s‖ ^ 2 := by
      rw [hLapp, ← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hτ.inner_sum, EuclideanSpace.norm_eq,
        Real.sq_sqrt (Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => sq_nonneg _)]
      simp [sq]
    exact (pow_left_inj₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _) two_ne_zero).mp h1
  have hiso : Isometry L := AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm L hnorm
  have hrange : Set.range L = (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) := by
    ext y
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
      rw [hLapp]
      exact Submodule.sum_mem _ fun i _ => Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩)
    · intro hy
      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℝ).mp (SetLike.mem_coe.mp hy)
      exact ⟨(WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).symm c, by rw [hLapp]; rfl⟩
  have h := hiso.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (d := n)
  rw [EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, hrange] at h
  exact h.symm

subproblems.title: Extension of a test function on the parameter domain of a plane to an ambient test function
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i, and Ω := {s ∈ ℝ^n : ι(s) ∈ V}. Let ψ : ℝ^n → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ Ω. Then there is a C^∞ function f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V such that, for every s ∈ ℝ^n, f(ι(s)) = ψ(s) and Df(ι(s))(τ_j) = Dψ(s)(e_j) for every j, where e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝ^n and Df(y)(v) = fderiv ℝ f y v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P) (ψ : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen V → Orthonormal ℝ τ → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → tsupport ψ ⊆ {s : Euclid n | ∑ i, s i • τ i ∈ V} → ∃ f : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ V ∧ ∀ s : Euclid n, f (∑ i, s i • τ i) = ψ s ∧ ∀ j : Fin n, fderiv ℝ f (∑ i, s i • τ i) (τ j) = fderiv ℝ ψ s (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent-supplied proof, construction of the ambient test function: "Since ι(spt ψ) is a compact subset of the open set V, there is δ > 0 with {y ∈ ℝ^P : ι^*(y) ∈ spt ψ, |y − p_Q(y)| ≤ δ} ⊆ V, where ι^*(y) := (⟨y, τ_1⟩, …, ⟨y, τ_n⟩) and p_Q is the orthogonal projection onto Q. With χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P), χ = 1 near 0, spt χ ⊆ B_δ(0), put f(y) := ψ(ι^*(y))·χ(y − p_Q(y)): f ∈ C^∞_c(V), f(ι(s)) = ψ(s) and D_{τ_i}f(ι(s)) = ∂_iψ(s)". Notation: ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm; B(0, ρ), B̄(0, ρ) are open and closed balls; cthickening δ A := {y : inf_{a∈A}‖y − a‖ ≤ δ}.
1. (Linear maps.) ι is linear and ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖ (orthonormality: ‖Σ s_iτ_i‖² = Σ s_i²). Let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^n, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_1, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_n, y⟩), a continuous linear map; let p := ι∘ι* (the orthogonal projection onto Q = span{τ_i}) and q := id − p, both continuous linear. By orthonormality, ι*(ι(s)) = s (⟨τ_k, Σ_i s_iτ_i⟩ = s_k) and ι*(τ_j) = e_j; consequently q(ι(s)) = ι(s) − ι(ι*(ι(s))) = 0, and every y satisfies y = p(y) + q(y) with ‖p(y)‖ = ‖ι*(y)‖.
2. (Margin.) K := tsupport ψ is compact (ψ has compact support) and K ⊆ Ω, so ι(K) is compact (ι continuous) and ι(K) ⊆ V. Since V is open, there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ (ι(K)) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Let R ≥ 0 with K ⊆ B̄(0, R) (K is bounded).
3. (Cutoff.) Let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be a smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius δ/2 and outer radius δ (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = δ/2 < rOut = δ): χ is C^∞, χ = 1 on B̄(0, δ/2) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall), and the support of χ is B(0, δ) (ContDiffBump.support_eq).
4. (Definition.) f(y) := ψ(ι*(y))·χ(q(y)). f is C^∞: ψ∘ι* and χ∘q are compositions of C^∞ functions with continuous linear maps, and products of C^∞ functions are C^∞.
5. (Support.) If f(y) ≠ 0 then ψ(ι*(y)) ≠ 0, so ι*(y) ∈ K, and χ(q(y)) ≠ 0, so ‖q(y)‖ < δ. Hence support f ⊆ A := {y : ι*(y) ∈ K and ‖q(y)‖ ≤ δ}. A is closed (K is closed; ι*, q and the norm are continuous), so tsupport f ⊆ A. A is bounded: for y ∈ A, ‖y‖ ≤ ‖p(y)‖ + ‖q(y)‖ = ‖ι*(y)‖ + ‖q(y)‖ ≤ R + δ. So A is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^P) and f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact). For y ∈ A, p(y) = ι(ι*(y)) ∈ ι(K) and ‖y − p(y)‖ = ‖q(y)‖ ≤ δ, so y ∈ cthickening δ (ι(K)) ⊆ V. Hence tsupport f ⊆ A ⊆ V.
6. (Values on Q.) For s ∈ ℝ^n: ι*(ι(s)) = s and q(ι(s)) = 0, so f(ι(s)) = ψ(s)·χ(0) = ψ(s) (0 ∈ B̄(0, δ/2)).
7. (Derivatives on Q.) Fix s ∈ ℝ^n. Since q is continuous and q(ι(s)) = 0, the set N := {y : q(y) ∈ B̄(0, δ/2)} is a neighbourhood of ι(s), and on N, χ(q(y)) = 1, so f = ψ∘ι* on N. Functions that agree near a point have the same derivative there (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so by the chain rule Df(ι(s)) = D(ψ∘ι*)(ι(s)) = Dψ(ι*(ι(s)))∘ι* = Dψ(s)∘ι*. Therefore Df(ι(s))(τ_j) = Dψ(s)(ι*(τ_j)) = Dψ(s)(e_j) for every j (step 1). ∎

subproblems.title: An approximate tangent plane of M lies in every subspace along which a set carrying H^n-almost all of M is flat
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and M, N ⊆ ℝ^P with H^n(M ∖ N) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] is the normalized n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure. No measurability of M or N is assumed. Let x ∈ ℝ^P, and let Q, T be linear subspaces of ℝ^P. Suppose N is flat at x along T: for every real ε > 0 there is a real ρ > 0 such that every z ∈ N with |z − x| < ρ admits some t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|. Suppose Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q). That is, finrank Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r ↓ 0 (along 𝓝[>] 0), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x). Then Q ⊆ T, i.e. Q ≤ T as submodules. Norms and distances are Euclidean.

The flatness established in its step 2 is now a hypothesis, T is an arbitrary linear subspace, and x need not lie in N. The resulting inclusion T_xM ⊆ T_xN is used in Ch. 4, 2.6–2.7 (book/chapter-04.txt lines 175–209).
Notation: H^n := μHE[n]. η_r(y) := r⁻¹(y − x), which is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r y. |·| is the Euclidean norm. B(a, s) and B̄(a, s) are the open and closed balls. dist(q, T) := inf over t ∈ T of |q − t| (Metric.infDist q T).
1. Set-up for contradiction. Let q ∈ Q; we show q ∈ T. Suppose q ∉ T. T is a finite-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and it is nonempty since 0 ∈ T. Therefore δ := dist(q, T) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos).
2. Test function. Let g(y) := max(0, δ/2 − |y − q|).
- g is continuous and g ≥ 0.
- If g(y) ≠ 0 then |y − q| < δ/2; otherwise δ/2 − |y − q| ≤ 0 and g(y) = 0. Conversely, |y − q| < δ/2 implies g(y) > 0.
- Hence g vanishes outside the compact ball B̄(q, δ/2), so g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
- So g defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), the CompactlySupportedContinuousMap ⟨⟨g, continuity⟩, compact support⟩, with f(y) = g(y) for all y.
The parent normalizes |q| = 1 and uses ε = δ/8 and r < ρ/2. Here no normalization is made and the constants of step 4 are used instead; the mathematics is the same.
3. ∫_Q g dH^n > 0. By hypothesis finrank Q = n.
(a) The measure H^n⌞Q is regular (SimonGMT Chapter03 regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), in particular finite on compact sets. So the continuous, compactly supported g is H^n⌞Q-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
(b) The support of the measure H^n⌞Q is exactly Q (SimonGMT support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule). Since q ∈ Q and B(q, δ/2) is a neighbourhood of q, (H^n⌞Q)(B(q, δ/2)) > 0 (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall, whose explicit argument is the point q).
(c) B(q, δ/2) ⊆ {g ≠ 0}, so (H^n⌞Q)({g ≠ 0}) > 0. Since g ≥ 0 is integrable, ∫_Q g dH^n > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg).
4. Constants. |q| + δ > 0. Put ε := δ/(2(|q| + δ)) > 0, so that ε(|q| + δ) = δ/2. Let ρ > 0 be given by the flatness hypothesis for this ε: every z ∈ N with |z − x| < ρ admits t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|.
5. Vanishing of the blow-up integrals. Fix r with 0 < r < ρ/(|q| + δ). We show ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n = 0.
(a) H^n(η_r(M ∖ N)) = 0.
- η_r(M ∖ N) = r⁻¹·A, where A := {y − x : y ∈ M ∖ N} (Set.image_smul, Set.image_image).
- The translation y ↦ y − x is an isometry (dist_sub_right), so H^n(A) = H^n(M ∖ N) = 0 (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- Since r⁻¹ ≠ 0, H^n(r⁻¹·A) = |r⁻¹|^n·H^n(A) = 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
(b) {g ≠ 0} ∩ η_r(M) ⊆ η_r(M ∖ N). Let y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M and g(y) ≠ 0; it suffices to show z ∉ N. Suppose z ∈ N.
- By step 2, |y − q| < δ/2, so |y| ≤ |y − q| + |q| < |q| + δ/2.
- Since r ≠ 0, z − x = r·y. Hence |z − x| = r|y| ≤ r(|q| + δ) < ρ.
- By step 4 there is t ∈ T with |z − x − t| ≤ ε|z − x|.
- Then r⁻¹t ∈ T and y − r⁻¹t = r⁻¹(z − x − t). So |y − r⁻¹t| ≤ r⁻¹ε|z − x| = ε|y| ≤ ε(|q| + δ) = δ/2.
- Consequently δ = dist(q, T) ≤ |q − r⁻¹t| ≤ |q − y| + |y − r⁻¹t| < δ/2 + δ/2 = δ (infDist_le_dist_of_mem), a contradiction.
(c) {g ≠ 0} is open because g is continuous, hence Borel.
- By Measure.restrict_apply, which needs measurability only of {g ≠ 0} and not of η_r(M): (H^n⌞η_r(M))({g ≠ 0}) = H^n({g ≠ 0} ∩ η_r(M)).
- By (b) and (a), this is ≤ H^n(η_r(M ∖ N)) = 0 (measure_mono_null).
- So g = 0 almost everywhere for H^n⌞η_r(M) (ae_iff), and ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae).
6. Conclusion.
- Apply the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q to f: the function r ↦ ∫_{η_r(M)} g dH^n tends to ∫_Q g dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0.
- The interval (0, ρ/(|q| + δ)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). So by step 5 this function is eventually 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, and therefore also tends to 0 (Tendsto.congr').
- Since 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ, limits are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique). Hence ∫_Q g dH^n = 0, contradicting step 3.
- Therefore q ∈ T. As q ∈ Q was arbitrary, Q ≤ T.

The blow-up η_{x,r}(M ∖ N) is H^n-null: H^n is translation invariant and scales by |r⁻¹|^n.

Take ε = δ/(2(|q| + δ)) and 0 < r < ρ/(|q| + δ). Flatness of N at x along T makes g vanish on η_{x,r}(M ∩ N). So g = 0 H^n-a.e. on η_{x,r}(M) (restriction evaluated on the open set {g ≠ 0}), and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} g dH^n = 0.
The defining limit along 𝓝[>] 0 then forces ∫_Q g dH^n = 0, a contradiction. Hence Q ≤ T.

Since τ is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent) and spans Q, it is a basis 𝔟 of Q indexed by Fin n (Module.Basis.mk, or OrthonormalBasis.mk), and dim Q = n; likewise τ' is an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q, so it spans Q and is a basis 𝔟' of Q.

1. (The plane.) τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so Q = span{τ_1, …, τ_n} is a linear subspace of dimension n (finrank_span_eq_card). Being finite-dimensional, Q is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), in particular Borel.
2. (Almost every point of M lies in Q.) (H^n⌞M)(ℝ^P ∖ Q) = H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0, so x ∈ Q for H^n⌞M-a.e. x.
3. (Approximate tangent planes.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n⌞M-a.e. x there is a linear subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q_x. Intersecting with step 2, fix from now on a point x of the full-measure set where both hold and x ∈ Q. By the definition of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt, finrank Q_x = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_{Q_x} f dH^n as r ↓ 0.

The map η_{x,r} is a similarity of ratio r^{−1}, so H^n(η_{x,r}(M ∖ Q)) = r^{−n}H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0. Hence f = 0 H^n-a.e. on η_{x,r}(M), and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n = 0 for every r > 0.

As q ∈ Q_x, (H^n⌞Q_x)(B(q, d/2)) > 0. The function f is continuous with compact support, hence H^n⌞Q_x-integrable, f ≥ 0 and f > 0 on B(q, d/2); therefore ∫_{Q_x} f dH^n > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg), contradicting (b). Hence Q_x ⊆ Q.

6. (Sign.) Let ξ_Q be the n-vector α ↦ α(τ) (evaluation at τ: linear in α and continuous, |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·Π_i|τ_i| = ‖α‖; in Lean the continuous linear map (ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply ℝ (fun _ => Euclid P) ℝ τ).comp (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toContinuousMultilinearMapCLM ℝ)). ξ_Q is a unit orientation of Q: IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_Q Q holds with the orthonormal family τ itself, span(range τ) = Q and the sign +. By steps 3 and 5, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q as well. Hence ξ(x) = ξ_Q or ξ(x) = −ξ_Q, i.e. ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for every α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for every α.
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 3–6 apply to H^n⌞M-a.e. x, which is the assertion. (The argument does not use n ≥ 1: for n = 0, Q = {0} and every n-dimensional subspace is {0}.) ∎

subproblems.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current equals its representing measure, and its support is the support of that measure
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be open, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), where H^n = μHE[n]). Write μ_R := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M. Then: (a) M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ U, where M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum (in [0, ∞]) of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; (b) for every x ∈ U: x ∈ spt T if and only if μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0; (c) every other representation R' of T has the same measure: R'.measure = R.measure.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.8 and Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 224–300 and 733–775), which state these facts as evident; this is the identity "μ_S = R.measure for every representation R, M_W(S) = μ_S(W), spt S = spt μ_S" used throughout the parent proof (its Notation paragraph). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing multi-indices I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) (for n = 0, |α| = |α()|); dx^I is the dual basis covector.
1. (Pointwise duality.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let α be an n-covector. By multilinearity and alternation, α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where τ^I is the n × n matrix (⟨e_{i_a}, τ_b⟩)_{a,b}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = det(I_n) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, with equality for α_τ := Σ_I det(τ^I) dx^I, which satisfies |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1. (For n = 0 both sides equal |α()| and α_τ := 1.)
2. (Consequences for R.) By the field `orients` of IMRep, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) and a sign σ(x) ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ(x)·α(τ(x)) for every n-covector α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Hence, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α. Moreover β(x) := Σ_I ξ(x)(dx^I)·dx^I equals σ(x)·α_{τ(x)} for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 there. The coefficients ξ(·)(dx^I) of β are H^n⌞M-measurable because ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^n⌞M (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient); as μ_R ≪ H^n⌞M, β is μ_R-measurable.
3. (Radon property.) μ_R is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U) and μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (field locallyIntegrable_mult). Since U is an open subset of ℝ^P, hence σ-compact, locally compact and second countable, the restriction of μ_R to U is a locally finite Borel measure on U and therefore outer regular by open sets and inner regular by compact sets on Borel subsets of U.
4. (Upper bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open and let ω be admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere). By R.Represents T and step 2, T(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_M θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n = μ_R(W), because ω vanishes off W. Taking ofReal and the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound in (a).) Let W ⊆ U be open, K ⊆ W compact and ε > 0. By step 3 choose an open V with K ⊆ V, closure V compact and contained in W, and μ_R(V ∖ K) < ε. By Lusin's theorem (for the finite Radon measure μ_R⌞V and the μ_R-measurable map β of step 2, with values in the finite-dimensional space Λ^n of n-covectors) choose a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < ε and β|_{K'} continuous. Extend β|_{K'} to a continuous map ℝ^P → Λ^n (Tietze, coordinatewise) and compose with the retraction r(α) := α / max(1, |α|) (continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball) to obtain a continuous β̃ with |β̃| ≤ 1 and β̃ = β on K'. Take χ ∈ C_c(V; [0, 1]) with χ = 1 on K, and put γ := χ·β̃ (continuous, |γ| ≤ 1, compact support in V). Let γ_j := γ * ϱ_{1/j} be the coordinatewise convolution with a standard mollifier. For all large j, γ_j is C^∞, tsupport γ_j is a compact subset of V ⊆ W ⊆ U, |γ_j| ≤ 1 everywhere (Jensen's inequality for the convex function |·|), and γ_j → γ uniformly. So γ_j is admissible for M_W(T) and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(γ_j). By dominated convergence (dominating function θ·1_{closure V}, integrable by step 3), T(γ_j) = ∫_M θ·ξ(γ_j) dH^n → ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n. On K', ξ(γ) = ξ(β) = 1 μ_R-a.e.; on V ∖ K', |ξ(γ)| ≤ 1; off V, γ = 0. Hence ∫_M θ·ξ(γ) dH^n ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(V ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − ε) − 2ε, since μ_R(V ∖ K') ≤ μ_R(V ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K') < 2ε. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3ε for every compact K ⊆ W and every ε > 0, and inner regularity of μ_R on the open set W (step 3) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
6. ((b), "if".) Let x ∈ U with μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0, and suppose x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T). Then x ∈ W for some open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes, i.e. T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Every admissible value in the definition of M_W(T) is ofReal 0 = 0 (and the zero form is admissible), so M_W(T) = 0, and by (a) μ_R(W) = 0. For ε > 0 so small that B_ε(x) ⊆ W we get μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ spt T.
7. ((b), "only if".) Let x ∈ spt T and suppose μ_R(B_ε(x)) = 0 for some ε > 0. Choose ε' ∈ (0, ε) with closedBall x ε' ⊆ U (U is open). W := B_{ε'}(x) is open, its closure closedBall x ε' is compact and contained in U, and for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, step 2 gives |T(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ·|ω| dH^n ≤ (sup_x |ω(x)|)·μ_R(W) = 0. So T vanishes on W, W belongs to the family defining zeroRegion(T), x ∈ zeroRegion(T), i.e. x ∉ spt T: a contradiction. Hence μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0.
8. ((c).) Let R' be another representation of T. By (a) applied to R and to R', R'.measure(W) = M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ U. Both measures vanish on ℝ^P ∖ U (both carriers lie in U) and are finite on every open W whose closure is a compact subset of U (step 3). The open subsets of U with compact closure in U form a π-system (closed under finite intersections) generating the Borel σ-algebra of U (every open subset of U is a countable union of them), and U is the union of an increasing sequence of them on which both measures are finite. By the uniqueness theorem for measures agreeing on such a generating π-system, R'.measure(A ∩ U) = R.measure(A ∩ U) for every Borel A, hence R'.measure = R.measure.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet duality: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for the unit simple orientation ξ(x), with equality for the dual covector β(x).
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) directly from the representation.
Lower bound by Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction to the unit ball, mollification and inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_R.
Support: T vanishes on W ⇔ M_W(T) = 0 ⇔ μ_R(W) = 0, giving spt T = spt μ_R inside U.
Representation independence: two representations agree on open subsets of U, hence (π-system uniqueness, σ-finiteness on U) everywhere.

3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).

subproblems.title: Signed integer density of an integer multiplicity current supported in an n-plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(V) an integer multiplicity current (IsIntegerMultiplicity S) with spt S ⊆ Q. Then there is g : ℝ^P → ℝ such that, with H^n = μHE[n] and |g(x)| read as the extended norm ‖g x‖ₑ ∈ [0, ∞]: (i) g is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞Q; (ii) g(x) ∈ ℤ for H^n⌞Q-a.e. x; (iii) ∫_{K∩Q} |g| dH^n < ∞ (lower Lebesgue integral) for every compact K ⊆ V; (iv) S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V); (v) M_W(S) = S.massOn W = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n for every open W ⊆ V.

Source: steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1–3.2 and the proof of the Constancy Theorem 2.34): the representation S = τ(M, θ, ξ), the carrier lying in Q, the orientation ±ξ_Q, and the signed integer density g := 1_M·ε·θ with μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α, α(τ) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n); |g(x)| := ‖g x‖ₑ; 1_A is the indicator function of A.
1. (Representation.) Since S is integer multiplicity, choose R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep V n with R.Represents S. Thus M ⊆ V is Borel, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M, ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V (field locallyIntegrable_mult), ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M, and S(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V). Let μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ.
2. (Mass, supplied step 1.) By the accepted sibling dimred_im_mass_measure (part (a); V is open and R represents S), M_W(S) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ V.
3. (Carrier in the plane, supplied step 2.) H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0. Indeed, by the accepted sibling imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (V open, R represents S), H^n(M ∖ spt S) = 0, and M ∖ Q ⊆ M ∖ spt S because spt S ⊆ Q. [Equivalently, by the supplied argument: every x ∈ V ∖ Q lies outside spt S, so by dimred_im_mass_measure (b) it has a ball of μ-measure 0; by Lindelöf countably many such balls cover V ∖ Q, so μ(V ∖ Q) = 0, and H^n(M ∖ Q) ≤ μ(M ∖ Q) ≤ μ(V ∖ Q) = 0 because θ ≥ 1 on M ⊆ V.]
4. (Orientation, supplied step 4.) By the sibling child planar_orientation_sign (idtp_pc_orient_ae_eq_or_neg) applied to R, τ and step 3: for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Call such points x good. As M is measurable, the set of x ∈ M that are not good is H^n-null; equivalently, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P, x ∈ M implies that x is good (ae_restrict_iff').
5. (Sign function.) Fix an n-covector β₀ with β₀(τ) = 1: let δ be the determinant n-form of ℝ^n (δ(c_1, …, c_n) = det of the matrix with columns c_j; continuous, n-linear and alternating; δ(e_1, …, e_n) = 1), let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^n, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_1, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_n, y⟩) (continuous linear), and put β₀(w_1, …, w_n) := δ(ι*w_1, …, ι*w_n), i.e. β₀(w) = det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_{i,j}; then β₀(τ) = δ(e_1, …, e_n) = 1 because ι*(τ_j) = e_j by orthonormality (for n = 0, β₀ is the constant 1). Put ε(x) := ξ(x)(β₀). Then ε is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M (composition of ξ with the continuous linear evaluation at β₀), and at every good x: ε(x) = ±β₀(τ) = ±1, ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}, and ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)·α(τ) for every n-covector α.
6. (Definition of g, supplied step 5.) Let g := 1_M·θ·ε, i.e. g(x) = θ(x)ε(x) for x ∈ M and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ M. By steps 4 and 5, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P: (a) g(x) ∈ ℤ (g(x) = ±θ(x) at good points of M, g(x) = 0 off M); (b) |g(x)| = 1_M(x)θ(x); (c) if x ∈ M then θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = g(x)α(τ) for every α.
7. ((i)–(iii).) (i): θ is measurable and ε is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M, so θε is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M; as M is measurable, its extension by 0, which is g, is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff), hence for H^n⌞Q. (ii): 6(a) holds H^n-a.e., hence H^n⌞Q-a.e. (iii): for compact K ⊆ V, by 6(b), ∫_{K∩Q} |g| dH^n ≤ ∫_K |g| dH^n = ∫_K 1_M θ dH^n = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ (step 1).
8. ((iv), the current identity.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) and F(x) := g(x)·ω(x)(τ). By step 1, S(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^P} 1_M θ ξ(ω) dH^n, and ∫_{V∩Q} F dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^P} 1_{V∩Q} F dH^n. The two integrands agree H^n-a.e.: at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M we have x ∈ Q (step 3) and x ∈ V (M ⊆ V), so both equal θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) = g(x)ω(x)(τ) by 6(c); at x ∉ M the first is 0 and the second is 0 as well, since g(x) = 0. Functions that agree a.e. have the same Bochner integral (no integrability is needed for this), so S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)ω(x)(τ) dH^n(x).
9. ((v), the mass identity; supplied step 5's μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q).) Let W ⊆ V be open. By step 2 and the definition of μ, M_W(S) = μ(W) = ∫_W θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫_{W∩M} θ dH^n = ∫_W 1_M θ dH^n (withDensity_apply, W measurable; Measure.restrict_restrict; lintegral_indicator). By 6(b), ∫_W 1_M θ dH^n = ∫_W |g| dH^n. Finally |g| = 0 H^n-a.e. on W ∖ Q (g = 0 off M, and M ∖ Q is H^n-null by step 3), so ∫_W |g| dH^n = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n + ∫_{W∖Q} |g| dH^n = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n (lintegral_inter_add_sdiff with Q measurable). Hence M_W(S) = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n. ∎

subproblems.title: The coordinate covector e_j ⌟ det on ℝ^{m+1} and its values on the basis with one vector removed
subproblems.statement: For every m ∈ ℕ and j ∈ Fin (m+1) there is a continuous alternating m-linear form β on ℝ^{m+1} (β ∈ Covector (Euclid (m+1)) m) such that, for every i ∈ Fin (m+1), β evaluated on the standard basis family (e₀, …, e_m) of ℝ^{m+1} with e_i removed (Fin.removeNth i) equals (−1)^j if i = j and 0 if i ≠ j. (Concretely β = e_j ⌟ δ, the interior product of e_j with the standard determinant form δ of ℝ^{m+1}.)

1. Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).toBasis, the standard basis of ℝ^{m+1}; b l = e_l for every l (OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply; `funext l; simp [b]`). Let δ₀ := b.det, the determinant alternating (m+1)-linear map with respect to b (Module.Basis.det). By Module.Basis.det_apply, δ₀ c = det (b.toMatrix c), and b.toMatrix c is the matrix whose (r, l)-entry is b.repr (c l) r = (c l) r. Hence δ₀ c = det (Matrix.of fun r l => c l r) for every c : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^{m+1} (in Lean, after `rw [Module.Basis.det_apply]` the goal is closed by `congr 1`).
2. Continuity of δ₀. The map c ↦ Matrix.of (fun r l => c l r) is continuous, because each entry c ↦ (c l) r is the composition of the evaluation c ↦ c l (continuous_apply l) with the continuous coordinate projection EuclideanSpace.proj r, and a matrix-valued map with continuous entries is continuous (continuous_matrix). Composing with the determinant (Continuous.matrix_det) shows that c ↦ δ₀ c is continuous by step 1. Then for every C^∞ function f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V, and every index j, ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·Df(x)(τ_j) dH^n(x) = 0, where Df(x)(v) = fderiv ℝ f x v.

Since ∂S = 0 in V, 0 = ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = (−1)^{i−1}∫_{V∩Q} g D_{τ_i}f dH^n"; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 2.34, formula (2) (d ω_j = (D_j a) dx^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^n). Here the sign (−1)^{i−1} is absorbed into the choice of the constant (n−1)-covector, so that dφ(x)(τ) = Df(x)(τ_j) exactly. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; indices of τ run over Fin n = {0, …, n−1}; for a family w = (w_0, …, w_m), Fin.removeNth i w is the family with entry i deleted; α(τ) := α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}).
1. (Degree.) Since n ≥ 1, write n = m + 1. Then BoundaryVanishes S means S.boundary = 0, i.e. ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = 0 for every φ ∈ 𝒟^m(V) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply: ∂S(φ) = S(dφ), where dφ = exteriorDerivative φ belongs to 𝒟^n(V) because d preserves smoothness and compact support and tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ).
2. (A constant m-covector.) Let e_0, …, e_m be the standard basis of ℝ^{m+1}. By the accepted sibling coordinate_covector (dgcr_bwd_coordinate_covector) there is an m-covector β on ℝ^{m+1} with β(Fin.removeNth i e) = (−1)^j if i = j and = 0 if i ≠ j (explicitly β(w_1, …, w_m) = det[e_j, w_1, …, w_m]: if i ≠ j the family (e_j, Fin.removeNth i e) contains e_j twice; if i = j, moving e_j to position j costs j transpositions). Let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^{m+1}, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_0, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_m, y⟩), a continuous linear map; by orthonormality ι*(τ_k) = e_k. Define the m-covector α on ℝ^P by α(w_1, …, w_m) := β(ι*w_1, …, ι*w_m) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap). Then for every i, α(Fin.removeNth i τ) = β(Fin.removeNth i (ι*∘τ)) = β(Fin.removeNth i e) = (−1)^j if i = j, and 0 otherwise.
3. (Test form.) Let f be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V, and put φ(y) := f(y)·α (a constant covector times a scalar function). φ is C^∞, has compact support, and tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ V; so φ ∈ 𝒟^m(V).
4. (Exterior derivative.) For every x ∈ ℝ^P and every family w = (w_0, …, w_m), since f is differentiable at x and α is constant,
 dφ(x)(w) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·D[y ↦ f(y)α(Fin.removeNth i w)](x)(w_i) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·Df(x)(w_i)·α(Fin.removeNth i w)
 (the alternating-sum formula for the exterior derivative, SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply in Chapter06/Forms.lean, dφ(x)(w) = Σ_i (−1)^i·D[y ↦ φ(y)(Fin.removeNth i w)](x)(w_i), applied to the form φ, which is differentiable at x; for each i the scalar function y ↦ φ(y)(Fin.removeNth i w) equals f(y)·c_i with the constant c_i := α(Fin.removeNth i w), whose derivative at x is c_i·Df(x) (fderiv_mul_const)). Taking w = τ and using step 2, only the term i = j survives: dφ(x)(τ) = (−1)^j·Df(x)(τ_j)·(−1)^j = Df(x)(τ_j).
5. (Conclusion.) By step 1 and the hypothesis on S applied to ω := dφ ∈ 𝒟^n(V):
 0 = ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·dφ(x)(τ) dH^n(x) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·Df(x)(τ_j) dH^n(x),
 the last equality because the two integrands agree at every point by step 4. ∎

For r > 0 let B_r be a ContDiffBump centred at 0 ∈ ℝⁿ with rIn = r/2 and rOut = r; as a function ℝⁿ → ℝ it is smooth (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ B_r ≤ 1, B_r = 1 on B̄_{r/2}(0), and support B_r = B_r(0) (ContDiffBump.support_eq), so it is continuous with compact support and integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). The map ι is an isometry (orthonormality: ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖, ι linear), hence a closed embedding and therefore a measurable embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). Consequently, for every measurable A ⊆ ℝ^P:

2. ((a) Ω is open.) Ω = ι^{−1}(V) with ι continuous and V open.
3. ((b) Ω is preconnected.) Let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^n, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_1, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_n, y⟩) (continuous). [Reason, as in the supplied step 7: the mollifications φ_ε of φ are C^∞, have supports in a fixed compact subset of Ω for small ε, and ∂_iφ_ε → ∂_iφ uniformly, while h is integrable on that compact set; so ∫ h∂_iφ = lim ∫ h∂_iφ_ε = 0.]
7. ((e) integrality and transfer back; supplied steps 7 and 8.) Let c₀ ∈ ℝ with h = c₀ L^n-a.e. on Ω. By (ii) and (1c) (with A := ℝ^P), h(s) ∈ ℤ for L^n-a.e. s ∈ ℝ^n. Ω is open and nonempty (step 3), so L^n(Ω) > 0 (IsOpen.measure_pos); hence some s ∈ Ω satisfies both h(s) = c₀ and h(s) = m for an integer m (Measure.exists_mem_of_measure_ne_zero_of_ae). Put c := m ∈ ℤ; then c₀ = c, and g(ι(s)) = h(s) = c for L^n-a.e. s ∈ Ω = ι^{−1}(V). By (1a) and (1c) with A := V, g(x) = c for H^n⌞(V ∩ Q)-a.e. x, i.e. for H^n-a.e. x ∈ V ∩ Q. ∎
